title: When Doctors Treated Disease With Mercury
style: Stylized realistic 3D CGI animation still, high-end animated explainer look, Pixar-meets-realism, cinematic soft lighting, detailed skin, hair and fabric, expressive faces, shallow depth of field, no text, no letters, no gore, vertical 9:16 framing.

sections.name: When Doctors Treated Disease With Mercury

lines.prompt: A Renaissance doctor in black robes holding a glass vial of shiny silver liquid mercury up to candlelight, alchemy lab behind

lines: For about four hundred years, one of the most popular medicines in Europe was liquid metal.

lines.prompt: A nervous 18th-century man sitting in a steam box with only his head sticking out, a doctor feeding vapour into it from a small furnace

lines: Doctors used mercury to treat syphilis. Patients rubbed it on, swallowed it, or sat in boxes breathing in its fumes.

lines.prompt: Close-up of a sick 18th-century man with a pale face holding a handkerchief to his mouth, drooling, in a dim bedroom

lines: The side effects were brutal. Drooling, loose teeth, shaking hands, and damaged kidneys.

lines.prompt: A drunk Renaissance sailor laughing at a tavern table while a skeleton in a doctor's coat waits behind him holding a mercury bottle

lines: People even had a saying for it. A night with Venus, a lifetime with mercury.

lines.prompt: 1940s doctor in a white coat holding up a small glass vial of penicillin in a bright hospital, nurses smiling

lines: It finally stopped in the 1940s, when penicillin arrived and cured syphilis properly.

lines.prompt: A modern doctor holding a broken old mercury thermometer with tweezers, placing it carefully into a hazardous waste container

lines: Today, mercury is so toxic that even a broken thermometer gets special cleanup.
